title: Home Was the Easy Part
author: GatorVault Staff
excerpt: Florida is 2-0 because the first halves were never close. The second half against Campbell is the game Auburn will play.
takeaways: The first halves made Florida 2-0. The second half against Campbell is the problem Auburn will play.
Seven flags after halftime (one in the first half, three in the whole opener) shoved drives into 1st-and-25. The offensive line took them.
Defense has not started a game yet. FAU was down-and-distance and tempo. Campbell was the first drive, then they settled. Still no three-and-out to open.
Philo went 16-of-21 in each game (517 yards, five touchdowns, one interception combined). Baugh has the long run. The line and the other backs are not where Sumrall wants them.

At Auburn: play the first-half team for four quarters. If they put extra bodies near the line to stop Baugh, throw over them. Get to Byrum Brown early. Tackle Singleton, Koger, and Nimrod after the catch.

body:
The Swamp wanted to party. Shop Boyz on the speakers, 52-3 on the board, the first 2-0 start in five years, and Jon Sumrall walking to the locker room like a man who still had work. Ten minutes later he said he was happy his guys got the win. Then he said the rest of it. A lot he was not pleased with. If Florida plays the second half the way it played the second half Saturday, they are about to have a real rude awakening. Walk into conference play like that, and they will get absolutely embarrassed.

The first half is the team people think they have. Florida went to the locker room up 45-3. Vernell Brown III had already scored twice on punt returns and once as a receiver. Dallas Wilson had the 40-yard touchdown. Jadan Baugh was running through a defense that could not stay in front of him. Aaron Philo was running the offense the way Sumrall asked him to, talking at the line, taking the snap that mattered. Offense, defense, and the kicking game were handing the night back and forth. That is complementary football. That is why the building sounded like a party.

Then the second half started, and Florida played a different game.

Every time they hit a big play after the break, another flag came out. The offensive line was the one taking them. T.J. Shanahan Jr. got called on back-to-back snaps. First a hold that wiped a Baugh run that was already gone. Then a personal foul. Roderick Kearney picked up another personal foul. A hold or a personal foul can shove you into 1st-and-25, first down with 25 yards still to go, and the drive is basically dead. In this league, Sumrall said, you might as well get ready to give the ball back. The Gators cannot beat the Gators. Seven flags after halftime. One in the first half. Three in the whole opener against Florida Atlantic. The first half can hide that. The second half put it on the grass.

The empty-bench snaps told the same story. Sumrall got people in the game, and some of those snaps told on people. Second-team and third-team guys got a chance to prove people right or wrong. Some of them, he said, proved why they are not playing. The standard is a Florida Gator standard, first team or third, and it is not negotiable. Freshmen have been here since January. Readiness is whether you can take the snap when your name is called. A few guys found out Saturday they are not there yet. That is the second half in a different uniform. When the script is no longer the first-half script, can you still play like this is Florida?

Defense has been living in that same gap for two weeks. They do not start games. After FAU, Sumrall watched the tape and said the issue was football IQ on the grass. Know the down and distance. Know when the other team is speeding the game up. Know when to crowd a receiver and when to give him a little space. On 3rd-and-short, a corner was sitting nine yards off the ball. That is too far. They kept FAU from hitting the long ones. They did not handle the pace. After Campbell he said it another way. The first drive got them, a couple of completions down the field, a field goal, then they settled in and held Campbell to those three points the rest of the night. He told the defensive backs not to get scared after a catch. At corner you are going to get beat. Next play. That was better. It was still not a three-and-out to open a game. They have not had one yet. Auburn will not give them a drive to find the game.

The parts that held are why 2-0 looks easy if you only read the score. Sumrall has said twice that Philo is running the offense. After FAU he said the interception was not on Philo, a catchable ball that should have been a completion, and that Philo talked at the line and led. After Campbell he said they are playing good football with him in the game. He went 16-of-21 against FAU and 16-of-21 again against Campbell. Add those two games together and that is 517 yards, five touchdowns, and one interception. Tramell Jones Jr. is still in the room. Philo has the starts because the first halves have looked like a quarterback who already knows the job.

Baugh is the same kind of clean. Last year his longest run was 23 yards. He has now hit a long one in back-to-back weeks, including the 75-yarder against Campbell. In two games he has 296 yards and five scores on 14 carries each Saturday. Sumrall likes the physical run and the long one. What he did not like is everything around him when the night got loose. The other running backs were sloppy. A guy went the wrong way. Somebody missed a block in protection. The first offensive line was not awful and is not where it needs to be. They did not open as many lanes for Baugh as they should have, and then they were the ones taking the flags. After FAU, Sumrall had been fired up about the receivers and tight ends blocking on the edge. After Campbell the line was the second half.

So Saturday is not a mystery. It is the first time the other team will not let Florida play two different games. Auburn does not care that Florida scored 118 points and allowed 24 in two home nights. Ole Miss, Missouri, South Carolina, Texas in Austin, and Georgia in Atlanta on Halloween are still on the card. Two blowouts do not move those games. The honest range for this roster is still 7-5 or 8-4 if the road weeks look like football. 2-0 is what you are supposed to be after FAU and Campbell. The only question that matters this week is which half shows up in Jordan-Hare.

Auburn is not the downhill run team people still picture. Their offense is no-huddle shotgun. They line up fast and almost never put the quarterback under center. Byrum Brown is the quarterback, the transfer who followed the staff. He wants his first option right now, the first receiver or the keep where he pulls the ball and runs it himself. Against Baylor he threw those short throws and let Keshaun Singleton, Jeremiah Koger, and Chas Nimrod catch it and run. When Baylor got to him late, he forced the ball and threw three interceptions. When they got in his face before he could find that first option, they sacked him five times. If Florida starts slow the way they have started two games, Brown will have that first option before the defense has found the night.

Auburn's defense will try to make Florida play the second-half version of itself. Their front is the defensive line and the linebackers stacked behind it. That group came downhill to stop the run. Baylor only got 103 yards on the ground. That is the trade. When you put extra bodies near the line to take the run away, you leave space behind them. Baylor threw for 333 yards into that space. If Auburn does that to Baugh, Philo has to throw over those extra bodies and finish the drive. If the flags come out after a big run, the drive dies at 1st-and-25 and the trade never happens.

Florida wins there if they play the first-half team for four quarters. Get to Brown before he finds that first option, and stay home when he keeps it. Tackle Singleton, Koger, and Nimrod after the catch. Start the game on defense. Keep the flags in the bag. The rest of it, Philo talking at the line, Baugh hitting the long one, Brown taking over a night, only matters if the second half does not give the game back.

Sumrall said he is a little uneasy with where they are. You can win games the way they have won these two. If they are not urgent and detailed this week, he said, Saturday will not be what they desire. Home was the easy part. The second half is the problem. Auburn will not let them play through it.
